mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations by raising discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with rising FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC over last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or Rank IC over last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate deteriorating consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC over last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (UNRATE < 4.0%), a month-over-month increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC over last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 (index 2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100.0, or Rank IC over last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%, or Rank IC over last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a tightening labor market, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or Rank IC over last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low interest rate regime (FEDFUNDS < 3.0%), a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals impending monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 3.0% and CPIAUCSL rises, or Rank IC over last 3 years is below 0.03.
